# Load the dataset and display the first few rows to understand its structure
import pandas as pd

df = pd.read_csv(DATA_PATH)
df.head()

# Display the column names and check for missing values in the dataset
df.columns, df.isnull().sum()

# Fill missing values in the 'revenue' column with the mean
df['revenue'].fillna(df['revenue'].mean(), inplace=True)

# Convert 'purchase_date' to datetime format
df['purchase_date'] = pd.to_datetime(df['purchase_date'])

# Aggregate revenue by month
monthly_revenue = df.resample('M', on='purchase_date')['revenue'].sum().reset_index()
monthly_revenue.head()

# Plot the monthly revenue to visually inspect for anomalies
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

plt.figure(figsize=(12, 6))
plt.plot(monthly_revenue['purchase_date'], monthly_revenue['revenue'], marker='o')
plt.title('Monthly Revenue Over Time')
plt.xlabel('Month')
plt.ylabel('Revenue')
plt.grid()
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.show()

# Calculate mean and standard deviation of the monthly revenue
mean_revenue = monthly_revenue['revenue'].mean()
std_revenue = monthly_revenue['revenue'].std()

# Identify potential canary values (more than 2 standard deviations from the mean)
canary_threshold_upper = mean_revenue + 2 * std_revenue
canary_threshold_lower = mean_revenue - 2 * std_revenue

canary_values = monthly_revenue[(monthly_revenue['revenue'] > canary_threshold_upper) | 
                                 (monthly_revenue['revenue'] < canary_threshold_lower)]

mean_revenue, std_revenue, canary_values

from statsmodels.tsa.seasonal import seasonal_decompose

# Remove the canary value from the monthly revenue data
monthly_revenue_cleaned = monthly_revenue[monthly_revenue['revenue'] != 1007251]

# Set the 'purchase_date' as the index for decomposition
monthly_revenue_cleaned.set_index('purchase_date', inplace=True)

# Perform seasonal decomposition
decomposition = seasonal_decompose(monthly_revenue_cleaned['revenue'], model='additive')

# Extract the seasonal and trend components
seasonal_component = decomposition.seasonal
trend_component = decomposition.trend

# Display the seasonal and trend components
seasonal_component, trend_component

# Calculate the average monthly revenue after excluding the canary value
average_monthly_revenue = monthly_revenue_cleaned['revenue'].mean()

# Calculate the seasonal effect by averaging the revenue for each month
monthly_revenue_cleaned['month'] = monthly_revenue_cleaned.index.month
seasonal_effect = monthly_revenue_cleaned.groupby('month')['revenue'].mean()

# Determine the maximum seasonal effect observed
max_seasonal_effect = seasonal_effect.max()

average_monthly_revenue, max_seasonal_effect
